extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, practitioners before the USPTO, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for imposing reciprocal discipline on a patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including service/response procedure, the conditions of suspension, publication/notice obligations, and administrative restrictions (Customer Numbers/PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a State authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; a Notice and Order is mailed notifying the respondent and giving an opportunity to respond under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order within the prescribed time (40 days here), and no genuine issue of material fact exists under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), reciprocal discipline is appropriate. The Notice and Order must be mailed (certified mail shown) and delivered; respondent is afforded the regulatory response period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of suspension terms mirroring state order
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO ordered suspension identical to the State order: two years stayed, with an actual thirty-day suspension and a two-year probation subject to conditions; reinstatement eligibility after thirty days subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline should mirror the state-imposed sanctions and conditions (including probation length and reinstatement prerequisites) provided the conditions of the state order remain applicable. Here, compliance with California probation conditions and passing the MPRE within the specified time are conditions precedent to the stayed suspension remaining effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to take and pass the MPRE as condition of reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed to take and pass the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE) within the time period specified in the California Final Order as a condition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing the MPRE is an explicit condition of the underlying state disciplinary order; reciprocal discipline enforces the same condition for practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, its duration, and the basis for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published Notice must identify the respondent, registration number, nature of the discipline (e.g., period stayed, actual suspension), and the factual and rule violations that led to discipline. The order here includes a sample Notice with factual summary of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation ensures other jurisdictions and public entities are informed of the USPTO action; the order directs OED to provide such notice following the discipline determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the order does not list § 11.58 duties verbatim, the reference requires disciplined practitioners to follow the enumerated post-discipline obligations in that regulation (e.g., client notification, handling of file matters, withdrawal obligations) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of respondent's name from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative action will remove the respondent's ability to represent clients electronically using those Customer Numbers/PKI credentials until reinstatement; this is a specific remedy to prevent practice while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall she have her name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition bars any circumvention of the suspension by acquiring or being placed on another person's Customer Number; reinstatement is required before any such privileges may be regained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of misconduct leading to state suspension (examples of unethical conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: The California suspension arose from failure to secure and file timely verified discovery responses, failure to advise clients of the need for verified discovery responses, failure to oppose motions to compel and for terminating sanctions, inaction, and failure to communicate with clients, which resulted in a judgment of dismissal and deprivation of clients' remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific facts illustrate conduct that violates professional responsibility rules (California Rules cited) and serve as examples of behavior warranting suspension: missed deadlines, inadequate client communication, failure to defend clients' procedural rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO disciplinary authority and procedure derive from federal statute and the implementing regulations; citation of these provisions is the legal basis for issuance and enforcement of the reciprocal discipline order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and response procedure for Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 was mailed by certified mail (with receipt number) and delivered; the Notice provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service (e.g., certified mail, documented receipt) and a specified response period are procedural prerequisites; failure to respond within that period supports a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists and permits entry of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to request reinstatement after actual suspension period
rubrics_metrics.description: After thirty days (the actual suspension), Ms. Nair is eligible to request reinstatement subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order mirrors the state order's reinstatement timing: following the actual suspension period, the disciplined practitioner may petition for reinstatement but must satisfy any conditions (e.g., completion of MPRE, compliance with probation terms) before being restored to practice.
